scientific_question: Why does quinoxalin-2(1H)-one react with methyl 2-diazo-2-phenylacetate to give the N-alkylated product selectively in dichloromethane under blue light? Develop and test an explanation of this selectivity.

inputs.content: Combine quinoxalin-2(1H)-one (0.25 mmol) and methyl 2-diazo-2-phenylacetate (0.625 mmol) in dichloromethane (2.5 mL) at room temperature under air for 3 h, irradiated by a 40 W blue LED at 467 nm approximately 2 cm away. No external photocatalyst or additive is used.
The N-alkylated product is methyl 2-(2-oxoquinoxalin-1(2H)-yl)-2-phenylacetate. It is reported in 72% isolated yield; only the N-alkylated product was observed under the reported conditions.
